correction.text: the Musi lowlands and South Sumatra without Bangka-Belitung, which the sultanate 'inherited sometime in the late 17th century' (Bangka Island page)

keyframe_review.note: 77,003 km2: 62 percent of South Sumatra province and 90 percent of Bangka-Belitung (gazetteer overlap). The Palembang page has no area and says the sultanate held territory 'from the Musi river delta to the Palembang city'; its present-day territory 'South Sumatra, Bangka Belitung, and parts of Bengkulu, Jambi, and Lampung' is the same order of size. The page is silent on the extent before 1659 (Tome Pires c. 1513 and the Demak refugee dynasty are on the page without years for the land): unverified within the budget. Bangka is removed before the late 17th century.

keyframe_review.note: 75,650 km2, almost the 1459 shape. Same adjustment; the page opened gives no dated change of land in 1512.

keyframe_review.note: 75,189 km2. The sultanate was proclaimed in 1659 (Palembang Sultanate page), inside this shape's years; the Dutch razed Kuto Gawang that year. No territorial change is dated.

74,958 km2. Bangka was 'inherited by the nearby Palembang Sultanate sometime in the late 17th century' and tin was found c. 1710, so Bangka-Belitung belongs to the shape from about this row's first year (the ledger puts the gain at 1670, confidence 1). Infobox area not given.
74,843 km2, valid for 1809-1811. Bangka was ceded to Britain in 1812 ('His successor ceded Bangka to Britain in 1812'), so the 1812-1819 years need the next keyframe; Cliopatria keeps Bangka to 1819.

correction.text: South Sumatra after the cession of Bangka to Britain in 1812 (exchanged to the Dutch in 1814)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1809 shape without Bangka-Belitung for 1812-1819, because Cliopatria drops Bangka only in 1820. Exact 1812 date not on the page; the Palembang page has the sultan deposed in 1812 (MBII's page: reign ended 14 May 1812).
54,607 km2: South Sumatra without Bangka-Belitung (zero overlap with Bangka-Belitung in the gazetteer). The state ends with the Dutch annexation of June 1821.

ledger.note: 1459: Palembang appears in the record as a Javanese-dependent principality (Cliopatria's first shape); the page dates no founding. It gives only earlier mentions ('Pa-lin-fong' in a Chinese chronicle of 1178; Tome Pires c. 1513 'a kingdom led by a patron appointed from Java'); the Palembang city page adds that Chen Zuyi was confronted there by Zheng He's returning fleet in 1407.

1659: Palembang is proclaimed a sultanate by Susuhunan Abdurrahman. 'It was proclaimed in 1659 by Susuhunan Abdurrahman'; the Dutch punitive expedition burnt the city that year, and the court moved from Kuto Gawang to Beringin Janggut.

region.text: Bangka (and Belitung): 'inherited by the nearby Palembang Sultanate sometime in the late 17th century'

ledger.note: Late 17th century: Bangka falls to Palembang by inheritance; tin is found c. 1710. The page gives no year: 1670 is the start of Cliopatria's row, the range is 1670-1699. Reviewer se-02-d: the Bangka Island page says Bangka 'continued to pass to the Banten Sultanate' before it was 'inherited by the nearby Palembang Sultanate sometime in the late 17th century', so the counterpart is Banten, not nobody.

region.text: Bangka: 'His successor ceded Bangka to Britain in 1812'

ledger.note: 1812: Bangka is ceded to Britain after Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II is removed (his reign ends 14 May 1812; he had massacred the Dutch post's staff on Bangka during the British invasion of Java in 1811). The island was renamed Duke of York Island.

region.text: the sultanate's remaining land, annexed by the Dutch

ledger.note: 1821: the Dutch take Palembang. 'The Second Expedition to Palembang in 1821 ended with the defeat of the Sultanate's forces ... annexed the city'; Mahmud Badaruddin II's reign ends 1 July 1821 and Dutch rule runs 'from June 1821'. The sultanate was formally dissolved 7 October 1823 (infobox), the last sultan Ahmad Najamuddin IV arrested in 1825.

wars.name: Dutch punitive expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: The Dutch burnt the city in 1659 and razed Kuto Gawang after a Dutch ship was attacked in 1657; the court moved to Beringin Janggut and the sultanate was proclaimed that year. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Palembang page: 'Tensions peaked in 1657 when a Dutch ship was attacked'; 'a punitive expedition in 1659, in which the city was burnt to the ground'. The Dutch company had a trade post since 1619 and the pepper monopoly since 1642.

wars.name: British invasion of Java and the 1811 Bangka incident
wars.outcome: Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II attacked and massacred the Dutch post's staff on Bangka in 1811; he was removed by the British and his successor ceded Bangka to Britain in 1812.
wars.note: The Palembang Sultanate page adds that a Dutch inquiry found no 'unquestionable evidence' that Raffles coordinated the 1811 attack.

wars.name: First Dutch expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: Dutch forces under Wolterbeek were defeated in 1819; fortified river coasts blocked a naval assault.
wars.note: 'resulted in the defeat of Dutch forces invading Palembang in 1819'.

wars.name: Second Dutch expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: The Dutch under Hendrik Merkus de Kock defeated the sultanate's forces and annexed Palembang in June 1821; the sultanate was dissolved on 7 October 1823.
wars.note: Led by de Kock against Mahmud Badaruddin II, who was exiled (to Ternate, where he died in 1852 per his page).

certainty.note: Riverine and coastal reach of a Musi-based state; no treaty line is dated by the pages opened.
The cession of Bangka (1812, confirmed by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814) is a dated transfer of an island; the mainland frontiers stay approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Sultanate of Palembang' 1459-1821 is one polity; the Wikipedia article starts the sultanate in 1659 (proclaimed by Susuhunan Abdurrahman). The dossier keeps Cliopatria's 1459 start, with a rename event in 1659; none of the four pages opened dates the earlier polity (a Demak noble, Geding Suro, 'established a new dynasty' with no year; the infobox lists the Demak Sultanate as predecessor but no land passed). The page does not call Palembang a vassal of Mataram or Banten; Cliopatria has no relation rows for it. The Malacca pages list Palembang among those that 'sent troops to the sultan' in 1511 (Capture of Malacca page); no vassal event is recorded.
Cliopatria's shapes put Bangka-Belitung in the state from 1459, but the Bangka page says it came to Palembang in the late 17th century, so the first three shapes are adjusted. The 1812 cession of Bangka is in the ledger; the 1814 exchange to the Dutch is in the Bangka page (a gain for dutch-east-indies, not a Palembang event). Belitung's history is not on any page opened. Cliopatria's 1820 shape (54,607 km2, South Sumatra only) drops Bangka-Belitung but keeps the same mainland cells as 1809. Dutch end: 1821 annexation (Cliopatria 1821); formal dissolution 1823, last sultan arrested 1825.
Page budget: 4 of 5 pages used; the pre-1659 history, the Mataram/Banten relation and the Lampung frontier are not covered.
Counterparts needing dossiers: Dutch East India Company (VOC) before 1800 (Dutch Republic's company; no Cliopatria row).
Disagreements: the sultan list dates (Abdurrahman 1704 or 1706; Mahmud Badaruddin I 1756-1758; Mahmud Badaruddin II 1803 or 1804 start; third reign from 1817 or 7 June 1818).
